 Joined 2026 Melbourne Korean Wave Expo
 Finance | Published 2026.11.08. 11:03:09 | By Kim Yeon-ha yeona@sedaily.com | Summary | Save A A A Visitors tour the booths of Kolmar Korea and its clients at the Korean Culture Expo held in Melbourne, Australia, from Nov. 5 to 7 local time. Photo courtesy of Kolmar Korea "K-beauty is drawing growing interest in Australia for its glass skin look and clean image. I came to the expo hoping to sign a formal import deal with a brand I've been watching," an Australian beauty buyer said.
 Kolmar Korea (161890.KS) said on the 8th that it took part in the 2026 Melbourne Korean Wave Expo, held over three days from the 5th in Melbourne, Australia, bringing six client companies with it. The event was hosted by the Ministry of Trade and Industry and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, or KOTRA.
 The client companies that joined were Goodai Global (Round Lab), Parket (Mixsoon), Mercico (Herbloom), iUnik (iUnik), Gibest (Nine Tales) and HK inno.N (Bewants). Kolmar Korea and the six companies held about 150 export consultations in total.
 Kolmar Korea's booth featured sunscreen, essences, creams and sheet masks. The company also ran a program that let visitors see for themselves how effectively its sunscreen blocks ultraviolet rays and test five sun care products, drawing a steady stream of buyers and visitors.
 "More than 10% of all consultations at the expo came from Kolmar Korea and our clients," a company official said. "Having confirmed the interest in the Australian market, we will keep working with our clients to widen local sales channels and actively support K-beauty's global expansion."
